subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Labetalol, Nifedipine, Aspirin and Chronic Hypertension in Pregnancy

steps.tx: The combined alpha and beta blocker first choice for severe hypertension in pregnancy is **labetalol**. Given intravenously in escalating boluses, it lowers pressure smoothly without reducing placental flow. Asthma and bradycardia are its main contraindications. Intravenous doses start at 20 milligrams and double every ten minutes to a usual maximum of 300 milligrams.
steps.say: Labetalol is first choice for severe pregnancy hypertension given in escalating intravenous boluses.

steps.tx: The calcium channel blocker used orally for acute severe hypertension and tocolysis is **nifedipine**. Immediate release capsules act within twenty minutes for pressure control. The same drug relaxes the uterus in preterm labour at different dosing. Sublingual nifedipine is avoided because the fall can be abrupt and hard to control.
steps.say: Nifedipine lowers severe pressure orally within twenty minutes and also relaxes the uterus.

steps.tx: Daily low dose aspirin from twelve weeks preventing pre-eclampsia is **low dose aspirin prophylaxis**. One hundred fifty milligrams at night is the dose supported by major trials. It works only when started before placental development completes. The ASPRE trial cut preterm pre-eclampsia by over 60 percent using 150 milligrams aspirin with first trimester screening.
steps.say: Low dose aspirin prophylaxis at night from twelve weeks prevents pre-eclampsia in high risk women.

steps.tx: Hypertension present before pregnancy or before twenty weeks is **chronic hypertension**. Superimposed pre-eclampsia complicates a quarter of cases and can be hard to recognise. Methyldopa, labetalol and nifedipine are the safe maintenance drugs. A rise of 30 systolic or 15 diastolic over booking values, with new proteinuria, signals superimposed disease.
steps.say: Chronic hypertension predates twenty weeks and a quarter develop superimposed pre-eclampsia.

steps.tx: Reversible brain swelling causing headache, seizures and visual loss in severe hypertension is **posterior reversible encephalopathy**. Imaging shows posterior white matter oedema. Pressure control and magnesium usually reverse it completely, hence the name. It is also called PRES, and blindness from occipital oedema is its most dramatic but reversible symptom.
steps.say: Posterior reversible encephalopathy swells the posterior brain and usually reverses with pressure control.

steps.tx: Methyldopa remains the drug with the longest fetal safety record for maintenance, termed the **safety standard**. Its slower onset makes it useless for acute severe hypertension. Sedation and positive Coombs tests are its quirks. It needs two to three days to work fully, so dose changes are judged over days, not hours.
steps.say: Methyldopa has the longest fetal safety record but acts too slowly for acute severe hypertension.

steps.tx: Drugs forbidden in pregnancy for hypertension include ACE inhibitors and angiotensin blockers, classed **fetotoxic antihypertensives**. They cause fetal renal failure and skull defects. Women conceiving on them switch immediately at the positive test. Enalapril in the second trimester can leave a baby with no urine output and unossified skull bones.
steps.say: ACE inhibitors are fetotoxic and women switch immediately at a positive pregnancy test.

steps.tx: Severe pressure in pregnancy is treated against the clock, but the landing zone matters as much as the speed. Aim to bring readings below 160 over 110 within thirty to sixty minutes of confirmation, using labetalol, nifedipine or hydralazine. Chasing a normal reading overshoots, because the placenta depends on maternal pressure for its own perfusion. These boundaries define safe **acute treatment targets**: fast enough to prevent stroke, gentle enough to protect the fetus.
steps.say: Acute targets bring severe pressure below one sixty over one ten within the hour without normalising it.

vis.caption: Severe pressure in pregnancy falling into the target zone below 160 over 110 within an hour, avoiding an overshoot that would starve the placenta. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Severe hypertension needs treatment within thirty to sixty minutes to prevent stroke, following **acute treatment targets**. The goal is a controlled fall to under one sixty over one ten, not normalisation. Over rapid falls compromise placental perfusion. Dropping mean pressure by more than about 25 percent quickly risks fetal distress from a pressure dependent placenta.
steps.say: Acute treatment targets a controlled fall within the hour, not normalisation of pressure.

steps.tx: White coat and masked hypertension distort clinic readings, resolved by **ambulatory monitoring**. Twenty four hour or home measurements guide true drug need in pregnancy increasingly. This avoids both overtreatment and missed chronic disease. Home monitors must be validated in pregnancy, because many oscillometric devices under read in pre-eclampsia.
steps.say: Ambulatory monitoring resolves white coat effects and guides true drug need in pregnancy.
